long_biography.plain_text:
After his father died, ten-year-old Constantin Keletsekis left Iran for Anatolia College in Thessaloniki. Athletics helped him settle into a school where Greek was initially more familiar in speech than in writing. He pursued higher education in Russia before returning to Iran in 1957 to take over his father's business interests.

Keletsekis built companies that delivered infrastructure across northern Iran and developed commercial fishing in the Persian Gulf and caviar production in the Caspian Sea. He also acquired Atlantic Gulf & Pacific, a US dredging contractor active in the Middle East and South America. The Iranian revolution forced his departure in 1979, when his holdings were nationalised. In Greece he served Anatolia College as a trustee. His reading ranged across Greek, Russian, English, French and Persian literature.
